title: Relative pseudo-coherence transfers between base and intermediate when the intermediate structure sheaf is pseudo-coherent
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For X -> Y -> S with X -> Y locally of finite type over S, and E in D(O_X), assuming O_Y is pseudo-coherent relative to S (i.e. Y -> S is pseudo-coherent, per the definition spelled out in the statement's footnote), the lemma says E is m-pseudo-coherent relative to Y iff relative to S. The retained proof is written: the question is local on X so all three affines; mimic the More on Algebra pullback-argument (cited by name) to factor X -> A^n_Y and embed A^m_Y -> A^{n+m}_S in the displayed cartesian diagram; the hypothesis on O_Y implies (via the chapter's base-change-relative-pseudo-coherent lemma, invoked as the author's example justification) that O_{A^m_Y} is pseudo-coherent relative to A^m_S, hence j_* O_{A^n_Y} is pseudo-coherent as an O_{A^{n+m}_S}-module; the equivalence then follows from the closed-immersion pushforward criterion Derived Categories of Schemes, lemma closed-push-pseudo-coherent. Retained author proof at lines 17248-17272.
